title: Western North Pacific winter surface lightened in 1990-2000, recovered in 2001-2006 and lightened from 2007; sigma0 26.5 O2 at 160 E-180 followed all three phases (WOD ship and Argo, 1950-2025)
abstract: Question: earlier work found that O2 on sigma0 26.5 at 160 E-180 began to fall near 1990, but that the western outcrop surface became lighter only near 2007. Did the O2 loss start before the outcrop changed? Approach: from 46 World Ocean Database files (ship and Argo, 140 E-150 W) we made annual late-winter 0-30 m series (92,076 casts) and isopycnal series (254,226 casts) with cell-season and year fixed effects and a cruise bootstrap, for fixed epochs E1 1975-1989, E2 1990-2000, E3 2001-2006, E4 2007-2025. Results: the surface of box W (36-48 N, 145 E-180) became lighter by 0.060 kg/m3 (95% -0.080 to -0.034) in E2, mainly by freshening at fixed temperature, recovered by +0.057 (+0.028 to +0.093) in E3 and became lighter by 0.122 in E4. Ships only, three other boxes, 1-degree cells and 36 epoch-limit choices give the same signs. The earlier no-change result came from epochs that left out 1994-1999; that study's own series shows -0.11 in those years. Within-type O2 on 26.5 at 36-46 N, 160 E-180 followed all three phases: -16.6 umol/kg (-24.7 to -10.9), +6.2 (+1.6 to +15.3) and -12.1 (-21.9 to -6.6). O2 follows the 3-yr W surface density with 147 umol/kg per kg/m3 (70-230; detrended surrogate p = 0.028), and a model fitted on 1955-1999 predicts the 2000-2025 epoch means (E3 -8.8 vs -8.2, E4 -21.7 vs -21.5). The 26.5 surface moved deeper by 39 m, shoaled by 17 m and moved deeper by 33 m in the same steps. Blind tests that the 26.4-26.6 layer thickness carries the signal failed: with Argo the thickness hardly changed in E2 and E3, and O2 does not follow it. Interpretation: the O2 loss at the western source started with a first lightening episode, so timing no longer argues against the outcrop explanation; the link is the density of the ventilated water, not the volume of the layer. Limitations: 1-6 O2 cruises per year in the region; epochs chosen after a look at published surface series (the O2 recovery and thickness tests are the independent parts); O2 tests were added after the thickness tests failed; few winter casts east of 170 E in 1990-2000; O2 change per unit lightening larger in E2 than later; arrival at CalCOFI not resolved.

citations.reason: Outcrop explanation and the 1989-1991 O2 onset at 160 E-180. This work shows a winter surface lightening in 1990-2000, which supports the outcrop explanation of the early loss; the layer-thinning part is not confirmed with Argo.

Uses its winter-cast method and annual series for reconciliation. Challenges its conclusion that the outcrop surface did not become lighter before 2007 and that the early O2 loss at 160-170 E needs another cause: its own series shows -0.11 kg/m3 in 1994-1999.
CalCOFI-band within-type O2 series for the downstream check; fixed-effects series method.
Equivalent density shift from winter surface lightening; this work finds that O2 follows surface density and isopycnal depth, not layer thickness.
Outcrop loss ahead of the CMIP6 forced path, half from freshening; this work finds a first freshening episode in the 1990s.
Within-type loss peaks on the classes that stopped outcropping.
Western O2 loss is regenerated, not a saturation change.
